feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows broad ownership across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally, but impact would be stronger with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a cleaner separation of projects from core experience.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of major digital functions.  
- Good credibility through concrete platform/scale details: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools.  
- Writing is polished and generally error-free, with strong domain-specific language suited to digital transformation and communications leadership.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope/activity: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, production savings, adoption rates, campaign results, or governance improvements.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve scannability and save space.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation/hyphenation varies (“front-end” vs broader style choices, “organization wide” should be “organization-wide” if used); “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization may look inconsistent unless intentional branding.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading modernization of” or “directing.”
- Add a concrete scale marker from recent experience to increase impact, e.g., “10,000+ page website,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related capabilities and reducing list-like phrasing.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Directs enterprise platforms, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal ecosystem serving 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The capability list closely mirrors Core Competencies; consider using the intro for positioning plus scale, not another skills inventory.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas and aligned more clearly to recent senior-level work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items into sharper, executive-level categories: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance, editorial systems & publishing operations • Analytics, reporting & optimization • AI-enabled search, automation & platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production, livestreaming & campaign delivery
- Replace “multi-channel communications operations” with “publishing operations” or “digital communications leadership” to sound more senior and specific.
- Keep parallel phrasing throughout; avoid mixing systems, outcomes, and channels in the same list.
- Consider ordering by current relevance: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, communications, multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” repeat language already used in the header.
- Several items also duplicate Topline Skills; this section should stay higher-level, not tool- or channel-specific.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent NACo roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, outcome-oriented verbs and specify impact where possible: e.g., “improving policy-content discovery,” “supporting ongoing campaign expansion,” “integrated with the main website.”
- Standardize style and punctuation: use sentence case consistently, hyphenate “bill-level,” and write “10 x 20-foot” or “10-by-20-foot” consistently.
- Consider this tighter rewrite: “Selected recent projects: AI Hybrid Search—Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat to improve discovery of complex policy content. We Are Counties Microsite—Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a modular architecture for future growth…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with recent Work Experience bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats across items; vary verbs to avoid monotony.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, strategic outcomes, and only the newest/highest-value work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web governance, campaign architecture, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Rephrase execution bullets to show outcomes: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits to support advocacy and engagement” and “Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search relevance gains, engagement/download metrics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Drupal microsites,” “AI-enabled search,” and “campaign storytelling” duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this item higher-level and let projects hold specifics.
- “Governance, analytics, workflows” also repeats the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize advisory/consulting scope rather than re-listing prior responsibilities.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals; it will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/result summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize highest-impact achievements first: Drupal migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, governance/operations improvements.
- Add outcome language where possible: site performance gains, publishing efficiency, reporting speed, cost savings from in-house production, engagement growth, or reduced reliance on vendors.
- Tighten channel bullet: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders” rather than listing generic platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo roles and footer projects; emphasize building the studio/capability, not recurring content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, cadence, cross-team coordination, and channel-building.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: newsletter ownership, launch/expansion of recurring advocacy video, and cross-functional editorial planning.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter send volume/open rates, video cadence/views, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated, or workflow time saved.
- Possible rewrite:
- Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and coordinated editorial execution.
- Owned four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Improved cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” is repeated in the Director role; keep this version more execution-focused.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership capabilities not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise web and communications strategy”; “Multi-channel communications leadership” → “Cross-channel communications operations.”
- Add one more distinctive capability tied to recent work, such as “Content governance and publishing standards” or “AI-enabled content discovery strategy.”
- Keep to 4 bullets max and use parallel noun phrases for cleaner scanning.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise web and communications strategy
- Content governance and editorial systems
- Cross-channel communications operations
- Public-sector advocacy and audience strategy

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and partly redundant with “editorial systems,” “communications operations,” and the header’s “content operations.”
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies; consider “public-sector advocacy strategy” if retained.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, not repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS leadership • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize the most current, proven strengths from recent roles: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/workflows.
- Remove lower-signal or less evidenced items here if space is tight, especially “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” and “Power Pages,” since they are already covered in Technical + IT.
- If you want more impact, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats Core Competencies almost verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools: “Analytics infrastructure and optimization” or “Analytics, reporting & performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” instead of listing each separately.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business language: “KPI framework development” and “executive reporting dashboards” are sharper than “KPI design” and “Leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive reporting dashboards • SEO, UX and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Performance analysis” may overlap with Core Competencies’ “Analytics and reporting infrastructure.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value production leadership and event delivery rather than basic task labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more outcome-oriented, senior phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production & post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ/multi-camera production systems
- Virtual event and advocacy content delivery
- Consider renaming the heading to “Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations” for clearer scope.
- Use “post-production” instead of “editing” and “multi-camera production systems” instead of just “PTZ camera systems” to sound more strategic.
- If space is tight, cut to 4 bullets and keep the most distinctive items: studio buildout, livestream/hybrid events, multi-camera systems, advocacy video delivery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies.
- Tool-level production details are also partially covered under Technical + IT (“Livestream studio workflows,” podcast production).

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either add context on level of use or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by depth/relevance: **Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping the title “Web Platforms & CMS” in favor of **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- Only keep platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; Drupal is clearly the strongest and should lead.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates the “Topline Skills” entry: **Drupal - WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages**. Differentiate this section with proficiency/context or remove one version.
- GitHub Pages is not reinforced elsewhere; keep it only if it supports a concrete project or technical positioning.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to capability-based phrasing: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless ATS targeting requires them; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., implementations supporting Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, or workflow automation.
- Order by strongest/current value: JavaScript • API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS • jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Google Tag Manager may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if that section needs more specificity.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize systems actually tied to recent leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Remove lower-signal tools unless actively used recently: **Basecamp, Trello**
- If accurate, add light context instead of pure listing: **Airtable (workflow systems), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (project operations), Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; keep this section tool-focused, not capability-focused.
- Collaboration apps like Slack/Teams can feel low-value on a senior CV unless framed as part of operational systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a generic tool list. Strengthen it by signaling enterprise-scale email/engagement capability and aligning wording with the more senior recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope-oriented phrasing elsewhere in the skills section, e.g. “enterprise email automation,” “newsletter operations,” or “member communications platforms” rather than just vendor names.
- Keep only the strongest/current systems; order by recent or most enterprise-relevant platform first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters” references in Work Experience; avoid restating channel ownership here.
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies unless tied specifically to email/member platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools for the target roles, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Use it to emphasize technical depth and methods rather than repeating the same list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Tighten and sharpen the content: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to recent impact, e.g. **Enterprise reporting** or **behavior analytics**, to better reflect the NACo director/consulting work.
- Consider replacing broad nouns like **Dashboarding** with more specific phrasing such as **KPI dashboarding** or **executive reporting dashboards**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly mirrors **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep this version tool-focused and let Topline Skills cover strategy/outcomes.
- Avoid repeating analytics platform names elsewhere unless paired with measurable results in recent experience bullets.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete outputs you can quantify.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and video operations.”
- Add measurable outputs if available: number of livestreams/events produced, frequency of video updates, size of web refresh, email volume, or team/process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and foreground outcomes: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” rather than implying broader management.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this at a tactical execution level.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch and frame the rest as program/policy support to keep the progression clear.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Supported innovation and research initiatives for NACo programs and policy teams, translating project work into digital and multimedia communications.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audience growth, stakeholder groups served, or types of research/projects coordinated.
- Tighten wording by removing vague phrases like “contributed to” and “materials”; use stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “managed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production; later roles already cover web, video, and multimedia leadership in much stronger terms.
- Don’t repeat “first podcast” elsewhere unless you can show broader organizational impact here.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only, not broad capabilities already proven elsewhere.
